title: System Too Rich Off Idle Bank 2
plain: The engine on bank 2 (the side of the engine opposite cylinder 1) is running too rich when driving just above idle, and the computer has reached the limit of what it can correct. Too much fuel or too little air is getting in.

causes.name: Leaking or stuck-open fuel injector
Fuel pressure too high (bad regulator)
Faulty mass airflow (MAF) or upstream oxygen sensor
Clogged air filter or intake

checks: Check fuel pressure and look for a leaking injector
Inspect the air filter and MAF sensor
fix: Find the source of extra fuel (injector, pressure regulator or sensor) and repair it.

title: Cooling System Performance
plain: The engine isn't reaching or holding its normal operating temperature the way the computer expects. Most often the thermostat is stuck open, but low coolant or a bad temperature sensor can do it too.
symptoms: Temperature gauge reads low or moves around

causes.name: Thermostat stuck open
Low coolant level or air in the system
Faulty coolant temperature sensor
Cooling fan running all the time
Coolant leak or failing water pump

checks: Check the coolant level when the engine is cold
Watch engine temperature in live data as it warms up
Compare readings from both coolant temperature sensors if equipped
fix: Most often a new thermostat; top off and bleed the coolant and test the temperature sensor too.
drive: Watch the temperature gauge. If it reads low or moves around, a stuck-open thermostat is likely and you can usually drive to a shop soon. If the gauge climbs toward hot, steam appears or you smell coolant, pull over and shut the engine off; overheating can ruin the engine.
test_first: Check coolant level, watch actual coolant temperature on a scanner as it warms up, and test the thermostat, temperature sensor and cooling fan before replacing parts.

title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit
plain: The engine computer has found a problem in the circuit for the engine coolant temperature sensor 2, which gives the computer a second reading of engine coolant temperature. It usually points to wiring, a connector or the sensor itself.
symptoms: Cooling fans may run all the time

causes.name: Faulty coolant temperature sensor 2
Damaged, corroded or unplugged connector
Broken or chafed wiring
Engine computer problem (rare)

checks: Inspect the coolant temperature sensor connector and wiring for damage or corrosion
Check the sensor power, ground and signal with a meter
fix: Repair any damaged wiring or connector first; if the circuit tests good, replace the coolant temperature sensor 2.

title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The engine coolant temperature sensor 2 is giving readings that don't make sense compared with what the computer expects. This sensor gives the computer a second reading of engine coolant temperature. The sensor may be failing or the system it watches may have a real problem.
symptoms: Cooling fans may run all the time

causes.name: Failing or out-of-calibration coolant temperature sensor 2
Low coolant or a stuck thermostat
High resistance in the wiring or connector

checks: Compare the coolant temperature sensor reading with related sensors in live data
Check wiring and connector for corrosion or looseness
fix: Confirm the system itself is working, then replace the coolant temperature sensor 2 if its readings are off.

title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit Low
plain: The signal from the engine coolant temperature sensor 2 is lower than the computer expects. This sensor gives the computer a second reading of engine coolant temperature. A wire shorted to ground or a failed sensor is the usual reason.
symptoms: Cooling fans may run all the time

causes.name: Signal or reference wire shorted to ground
Failed coolant temperature sensor 2
Corroded or damaged connector
Engine computer problem (rare)

checks: Inspect the coolant temperature sensor wiring for rubbed-through or pinched spots
Unplug the sensor and see if the reading changes, which helps separate wiring from sensor
fix: Repair any damaged wiring or connector first; if the circuit tests good, replace the coolant temperature sensor 2.

title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit High
plain: The signal from the engine coolant temperature sensor 2 is higher than the computer expects. This sensor gives the computer a second reading of engine coolant temperature. An open (broken) wire, a bad ground or a failed sensor is the usual reason.
symptoms: Cooling fans may run all the time

causes.name: Open or broken signal or ground wire
Unplugged or corroded connector
Failed coolant temperature sensor 2
Wire shorted to a power source

checks: Make sure the coolant temperature sensor connector is fully plugged in and clean
Check the sensor ground and signal wire for an open circuit
fix: Repair any damaged wiring or connector first; if the circuit tests good, replace the coolant temperature sensor 2.

title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
plain: The signal from the engine coolant temperature sensor 2 keeps dropping out or jumping around. This sensor gives the computer a second reading of engine coolant temperature. A loose connection or a damaged wire is the usual reason.
symptoms: Cooling fans may run all the time

causes.name: Loose or corroded connector
Chafed wire that opens or shorts as the engine moves
Failing coolant temperature sensor 2

checks: Wiggle the harness and connector while watching live data for dropouts
Inspect the coolant temperature sensor wiring along its whole route
fix: Repair any damaged wiring or connector first; if the circuit tests good, replace the coolant temperature sensor 2.

title: System Too Lean at Idle Bank 1
plain: The engine on bank 1 (the side of the engine with cylinder 1) is running too lean at idle, and the computer has reached the limit of what it can correct. Too much air or too little fuel is getting in.

causes.name: Vacuum leak (cracked hose, intake gasket or PCV valve)
Dirty or faulty mass airflow (MAF) sensor
Leaking intake manifold gasket
Low fuel pressure or weak fuel pump
Exhaust leak before the front oxygen sensor

checks: Listen and smoke-test for vacuum leaks
Inspect and clean the MAF sensor
Check fuel trims at idle and at higher RPM
fix: Find and repair the leak or fuel delivery problem; replacing parts without testing rarely fixes it.

cost.job: Find and repair vacuum leak (hose or intake gasket)

examples: Often appears with P2189 on V-type engines when a shared vacuum leak affects both banks
drive: Usually drivable while you arrange a check. If the check engine light is flashing, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off.
test_first: Smoke-test for vacuum leaks, check the PCV system, intake gaskets and fuel pressure, and review fuel trims at idle before replacing the oxygen or airflow sensor.
urgent_if: If the check engine light is flashing or the engine is shaking hard, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off. Don't keep driving; a heavy misfire can overheat and ruin the catalytic converter and leave you without power in traffic. Have it towed or checked right away.

causes.name: Leaking or stuck-open fuel injector

title: System Too Lean at Idle Bank 2

causes.name: Vacuum leak (cracked hose, intake gasket or PCV valve)
Dirty or faulty mass airflow (MAF) sensor
Leaking intake manifold gasket
Low fuel pressure or weak fuel pump
Exhaust leak before the front oxygen sensor

checks: Listen and smoke-test for vacuum leaks
Inspect and clean the MAF sensor
Check fuel trims at idle and at higher RPM
fix: Find and repair the leak or fuel delivery problem; replacing parts without testing rarely fixes it.

cost.job: Find and repair vacuum leak (hose or intake gasket)

drive: Usually drivable while you arrange a check. If the check engine light is flashing, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off.
test_first: Smoke-test for vacuum and intake leaks on the bank 2 side, check fuel pressure and bank 2 injectors, and compare fuel trims between banks before replacing sensors.
urgent_if: If the check engine light is flashing or the engine is shaking hard, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off. Don't keep driving; a heavy misfire can overheat and ruin the catalytic converter and leave you without power in traffic. Have it towed or checked right away.

title: System Too Lean at Higher Load Bank 1
plain: The engine on bank 1 (the side of the engine with cylinder 1) is running too lean under heavier load like accelerating or climbing hills, and the computer has reached the limit of what it can correct. Too much air or too little fuel is getting in.
symptoms: Hesitation or lack of power when accelerating

causes.name: Weak fuel pump or clogged fuel filter
Dirty or faulty mass airflow (MAF) sensor
Clogged or weak fuel injectors
Vacuum or intake air leak
Low fuel pressure from a bad regulator

checks: Check fuel pressure under load
Inspect and clean the MAF sensor
Check fuel trims at idle and at higher RPM
fix: Find and repair the leak or fuel delivery problem; replacing parts without testing rarely fixes it.
drive: Usually drivable with care. If you lose power when accelerating, it hesitates badly when merging, or it stalls, limit driving and get it checked soon. If the check engine light is flashing, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off.
test_first: Check fuel pressure and volume under load, the fuel filter and pump, mass airflow sensor readings, and for intake leaks after the airflow sensor before replacing parts.
urgent_if: If the check engine light is flashing or the engine is shaking hard, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off. Don't keep driving; a heavy misfire can overheat and ruin the catalytic converter and leave you without power in traffic. Have it towed or checked right away.

title: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Lean Bank 1 Sensor 1
plain: The front oxygen sensor on bank 1 (the side of the engine with cylinder 1) keeps reading lean and isn't responding normally. The sensor may be worn out, or the engine may really be running lean.
symptoms: Often no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Worn or contaminated front oxygen (air-fuel ratio) sensor
Vacuum or intake air leak
Exhaust leak near the front oxygen sensor
Dirty or faulty mass airflow sensor
Oxygen sensor wiring or heater problem

checks: Look for vacuum and exhaust leaks
Watch the front O2 sensor reading respond to a snap of the throttle
Check fuel trims and MAF readings
fix: Fix any leaks or fuel problems first; if the sensor is slow or stuck, replace it.
drive: Usually drivable normally while you arrange a check; fuel economy may drop. If the check engine light is flashing, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off.
test_first: Check for exhaust leaks near the front oxygen sensor and for vacuum leaks, check fuel trims and fuel pressure, and test the sensor's response before replacing it.
urgent_if: If the check engine light is flashing or the engine is shaking hard, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off. Don't keep driving; a heavy misfire can overheat and ruin the catalytic converter and leave you without power in traffic. Have it towed or checked right away.

title: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Rich Bank 1 Sensor 1
plain: The front oxygen sensor on bank 1 (the side of the engine with cylinder 1) keeps reading rich and isn't responding normally. The sensor may be worn out, or the engine may really be running rich.
symptoms: Possible fuel smell or black smoke

causes.name: Worn or contaminated front oxygen (air-fuel ratio) sensor
Leaking fuel injector
Fuel pressure too high
Dirty or faulty mass airflow sensor
Oxygen sensor wiring or heater problem

checks: Check fuel pressure and look for leaking injectors
Watch the front O2 sensor reading respond to a snap of the throttle
Check fuel trims and MAF readings
fix: Fix any leaks or fuel problems first; if the sensor is slow or stuck, replace it.
drive: Usually drivable short term. If you smell raw fuel, see black smoke, or the light flashes, get it checked soon, since running rich can foul plugs and overheat the catalytic converter. A strong fuel smell inside the car means stop driving.
test_first: Check fuel trims, fuel pressure, leaking injectors and the purge valve, and test the front oxygen sensor's response and wiring before replacing it.

title: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Lean Bank 2 Sensor 1

fix: Fix any leaks or fuel problems first; if the sensor is slow or stuck, replace it.

title: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Rich Bank 2 Sensor 1

causes.name: Worn or contaminated front oxygen (air-fuel ratio) sensor
Leaking fuel injector
Fuel pressure too high
Dirty or faulty mass airflow sensor

checks: Check fuel pressure and look for leaking injectors

title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 1/2 Correlation
plain: The vehicle has two intake air temperature sensors, and their readings don't agree with each other. One sensor or its wiring is usually at fault.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives
Possible small drop in fuel economy

causes.name: Faulty intake air temperature sensor (often inside the MAF sensor)
Faulty second IAT sensor (often in the intake manifold or MAP sensor)
Loose or corroded sensor connector
Heat soak after a short hot shutdown
Damaged wiring

checks: Compare both IAT readings in live data with the engine cold
Inspect both sensor connectors and wiring
Check for service bulletins for your vehicle (the Bulletins page explains what a bulletin is)
fix: Replace whichever IAT sensor reads wrong, which is often part of the MAF or MAP sensor.
drive: It usually doesn't change how the car drives; it rarely affects how the car runs. Get it checked when convenient. If other warning lights come on or the engine starts running poorly, have it looked at sooner.
test_first: Compare both intake air temperature readings to actual air temperature after the car sits overnight, check sensor wiring and connectors, and confirm which sensor is off before replacing.
